text: Theo’s fascination with the stars was not merely a childhood pastime but a profound emotional tether to his late mother, an astrophysicist who had nurtured his curiosity about the universe. From the rooftop of their rural home, he spent countless nights looking up, seeking answers in the celestial expanse. While he often pondered the mysteries of galaxies and black holes, there was one simple question his mother had answered with gentle clarity: she explained that the fluffy things in the sky, the clouds, were where rain comes from. This memory of her voice, calm and educational, grounded his lofty astronomical dreams in the tangible reality of weather and water, shaping his understanding that even the most distant wonders are connected to the earth below.
